task_1.title: Restore deprecated Flask Markup export compatibility
task_1.description: Flask 2.3.1 restores the deprecated `Markup` export on the `flask` package so legacy imports and attribute access continue to work instead of failing unexpectedly after upgrading to 2.3.0.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that applications upgrading to Flask 2.3.1 can still access the deprecated `Markup` export from `flask`, so legacy code using `from flask import Markup` or `flask.Markup` does not break unexpectedly.

expectation.grounded: The `flask` package should again expose `Markup` through its public package namespace. Both `from flask import Markup` and `flask.Markup` should resolve to the `Markup` type from `markupsafe`, while preserving the symbol's deprecated status.
expectation.conceptual: Codebases that still rely on the old `Markup` access path should keep running after the upgrade. The package should provide backward-compatible access to this deprecated symbol instead of failing during import or attribute lookup.

constraints.grounded: This change is limited to restoring the deprecated `Markup` alias in Flask's public namespace. It should not change the behavior of the underlying `markupsafe.Markup` type, promote the alias to a preferred API, or alter unrelated package exports.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be narrowly scoped to compatibility for legacy `Markup` usage. It should not change what `Markup` does or expand the library's public behavior beyond restoring the deprecated alias.

behavior: `from flask import Markup` succeeds again instead of failing because `Markup` is missing from the `flask` package namespace.
`flask.Markup` attribute access succeeds again instead of raising an attribute lookup error.
The restored `flask.Markup` export refers to the `Markup` type provided by MarkupSafe.
The restored export remains deprecated compatibility behavior rather than a newly introduced supported API surface.
acceptance_criteria: When an application executes `from flask import Markup` after upgrading to 2.3.1, it should receive a usable `Markup` type from the `flask` package.
When an application accesses `flask.Markup` after upgrading to 2.3.1, it should obtain the same usable `Markup` type instead of an attribute error.
When legacy code formats or wraps values using the restored `Markup` export, it should behave as the MarkupSafe `Markup` type rather than as a Flask-specific replacement.
When existing projects continue using this deprecated import path, the upgrade should preserve runtime compatibility without redefining it as the recommended API.
